_note: Test-only fake language: every English text with a marker in front. Never shipped.

OPEN_CIRCUIT.gap.title: «xx» The circuit is not complete
OPEN_CIRCUIT.gap.explain: «xx» Current can only flow around a full loop, from the + of the supply back to its −. Somewhere in your circuit the loop is broken.
OPEN_CIRCUIT.gap.fix: «xx» Follow the path with your eyes from the + terminal. Look for a missing wire or a loose end, then connect it.

OPEN_CIRCUIT.switch_open.title: «xx» The switch is open
OPEN_CIRCUIT.switch_open.explain: «xx» An open switch leaves a gap in the circuit, so no current can flow.
OPEN_CIRCUIT.switch_open.fix: «xx» Click the switch to close it.

SHORT_CIRCUIT.title: «xx» The supply is connected straight back to itself
SHORT_CIRCUIT.explain: «xx» A wire (or an ammeter) joins the + and − of the supply with nothing in between to hold the current back. This is a short circuit. In real life it can overheat wires and drain a battery in seconds.
SHORT_CIRCUIT.fix: «xx» Open the switch. Then check that the current has to pass through the resistor before it can get back to the supply.

AMMETER_PARALLEL.title: «xx» The ammeter is connected across a part
AMMETER_PARALLEL.explain: «xx» An ammeter measures the current flowing through a path, so it must sit in that path. Here it is side by side with another part (in parallel), so the current can skip around that part.
AMMETER_PARALLEL.fix: «xx» Take the ammeter out of the side connection and put it in the path itself, one after another with the resistor (in series).

AMMETER_NOT_IN_SERIES.title: «xx» The current does not pass through the ammeter
AMMETER_NOT_IN_SERIES.explain: «xx» To read the current correctly, all of it must flow through the ammeter. Right now some or all of it goes another way.
AMMETER_NOT_IN_SERIES.fix: «xx» Connect the ammeter in the main path, in line with the supply and the resistor.

VOLTMETER_SERIES.title: «xx» The voltmeter is in the main path
VOLTMETER_SERIES.explain: «xx» A voltmeter has a very large resistance. In the main path it blocks the current, and the circuit stops working.
VOLTMETER_SERIES.fix: «xx» Move the voltmeter so it connects across the part you want to measure, with one wire on each side.

VOLTMETER_WRONG_PLACE.single.title: «xx» The voltmeter is not across the resistor
VOLTMETER_WRONG_PLACE.single.explain: «xx» A voltmeter shows the voltage between the two points it touches. To measure the resistor, it must touch both ends of the resistor.
VOLTMETER_WRONG_PLACE.single.fix: «xx» Connect one voltmeter terminal to each end of the resistor.

VOLTMETER_WRONG_PLACE.combination.title: «xx» The voltmeter is not across both resistors
VOLTMETER_WRONG_PLACE.combination.explain: «xx» Here the voltmeter should measure the voltage across R1 and R2 together, so it must touch the two outer ends of the pair.
VOLTMETER_WRONG_PLACE.combination.fix: «xx» Connect one voltmeter terminal to each outer end of the R1 and R2 pair.

WRONG_POLARITY.title: «xx» A meter is connected the wrong way round
WRONG_POLARITY.explain: «xx» Meters have a + and a − terminal. Current should enter the + terminal and leave by the −. Here it is the other way round, so the needle tries to move backwards.
WRONG_POLARITY.fix: «xx» Swap the two wires on the marked meter so its red + terminal faces the + side of the supply.

MISSING_COMPONENT.title: «xx» A part is still missing
MISSING_COMPONENT.explain: «xx» Before you can take a reading, these parts need to be on the bench: {types}.
MISSING_COMPONENT.fix: «xx» Drag the missing part from the shelf onto the bench and connect it.

WRONG_TOPOLOGY.series.title: «xx» R1 and R2 are not in series
WRONG_TOPOLOGY.series.explain: «xx» In series, the resistors are joined one after another, so the same current passes through both. Yours are connected in a different way.
WRONG_TOPOLOGY.series.fix: «xx» Connect the second end of R1 to the first end of R2, then connect the two free ends into the rest of the circuit.

WRONG_TOPOLOGY.parallel.title: «xx» R1 and R2 are not in parallel
WRONG_TOPOLOGY.parallel.explain: «xx» In parallel, both resistors are joined between the same two points, so the current splits between them.
WRONG_TOPOLOGY.parallel.fix: «xx» Join the left ends of R1 and R2 together, and the right ends together, then connect those two points into the circuit.

MISSING_READING.title: «xx» You need more readings
MISSING_READING.explain: «xx» This task needs {need} readings at different voltages. You have {have}.
MISSING_READING.fix: «xx» Change the voltage on the supply, then press Record reading.

MISSING_ANSWER.title: «xx» Check your equivalent resistance first
MISSING_ANSWER.explain: «xx» You need a correct equivalent resistance before you can move on.
MISSING_ANSWER.fix: «xx» Work it out, type it in the box and press Check.

EQUIVALENT_R_WRONG.series.title: «xx» That answer is not quite right
EQUIVALENT_R_WRONG.series.explain: «xx» Your answer is more than 2% away from the correct value for resistors in series.
EQUIVALENT_R_WRONG.series.fix: «xx» For series, add the two resistances. Then try again.

EQUIVALENT_R_WRONG.parallel.title: «xx» That answer is not quite right
EQUIVALENT_R_WRONG.parallel.explain: «xx» Your answer is more than 2% away from the correct value for resistors in parallel.
EQUIVALENT_R_WRONG.parallel.fix: «xx» For parallel, use 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2. Then try again.

OK_CIRCUIT_COMPLETE.title: «xx» The circuit is complete
OK_CIRCUIT_COMPLETE.explain: «xx» Current has a full loop to flow around.

OK_AMMETER_SERIES.title: «xx» Correct: the ammeter is in series
OK_AMMETER_SERIES.explain: «xx» All the current passes through it, so it can measure that current.

OK_VOLTMETER_ACROSS.title: «xx» Correct: the voltmeter is across the right part
OK_VOLTMETER_ACROSS.explain: «xx» It touches both ends of the part, so it shows the voltage across it.

OK_POLARITY.title: «xx» Correct: the meters are the right way round
OK_POLARITY.explain: «xx» Current enters the + terminals, so the needles move forwards.

OK_TOPOLOGY.series.title: «xx» Correct: R1 and R2 are in series
OK_TOPOLOGY.series.explain: «xx» They are joined one after another, so the same current passes through both.

OK_TOPOLOGY.parallel.title: «xx» Correct: R1 and R2 are in parallel
OK_TOPOLOGY.parallel.explain: «xx» They are joined between the same two points, so the current splits between them.

OK_ANSWER.title: «xx» Correct answer
OK_ANSWER.explain: «xx» Your equivalent resistance matches the calculated value.
